Industries

Tax season picks the firm it can find

“Accountant near me,” “CPA near me,” “tax preparation” — the search for a numbers person happens on the map, and the answer changes across a city. Eagle Eye shows an accounting firm exactly where it ranks across its catchment and which competing practice is being found instead.

What a scan tells an accounting firm

  • Rank across the whole city — a grid of real search points, not a single position.
  • LSOV — the share of the area that sees the firm in the top 3.
  • Competitor maps — the rival firms taking the searches you’re missing, point by point.
  • Branded reports — a clean map and the numbers, with the firm’s own branding.

More than one office? Track each on its own grid. See what it costs.

Three numbers, every scan

Three numbers a client remembers and a trend that proves your work paid off. Every scan rolls the whole grid into them — no spreadsheet, no hand-waving.

Local Share of Voice
LSOVLocal Share of Voice

How much of the whole grid finds the business near the top — one number for the entire map.

Average Rank, found
ARPAverage Rank, found

The mean position across only the points that return the business at all.

Average Total Rank
ATRPAverage Total Rank

The same average, counting every point that missed the business entirely — the honest one.

Questions, answered

How does Eagle Eye help an accounting firm rank locally?

It runs a real “accountant near me” map search from a grid of points across the city, so you see where the firm ranks in the top 3 and where a competing practice is found instead — folded into LSOV, ARP and ATRP.

Can I track more than one office?

Yes. Each office gets its own grid and its own LSOV, so you can compare locations on the same numbers from one account.

Can I give a client or partner a branded report?

Yes. Every scan exports as a branded PDF or CSV with your own logo, colours and footer — a clean map and the numbers, ready to hand over.

What do LSOV, ARP and ATRP mean?

Every scan folds the grid into three figures: LSOV (the share of points where you rank in the top 3), ARP (your average rank where you appear in the top 20) and ATRP (the same average, counting every missing point as 21 so the blank parts of the map are measured too).

Can I try it free?

A new organisation starts with 10 free scans, and your first scan of your own website is free at any size up to 21 × 21 — no card needed.
